title: How Adam Robinson bootstrapped Retention.com to $22M ARR and pivoted to B2B via LinkedIn co-creation
summary: Adam Robinson recounts taking Retention.com from zero to $22M ARR with a tiny team, using outrageous Facebook ads, cold email and word of mouth. He covers the stalls, the failed 2023 scale-up, and the pivot to B2B, where LinkedIn content let him build a waitlist of ideal buyers before the product shipped.

principles.text: With strong product and one or two channels plus word of mouth, you can get much further with far fewer people.
principles.quote: with the right combination of product and then just one or two channels and word of mouth, you can get way farther than you think that you can get with way fewer bodies.

principles.text: Without word of mouth nothing accelerates growth; with it, many tactics work.
principles.quote: If you do not yet have word of mouth nothing that you do will work.

principles.text: Early on, be outrageous to cut through the noise; a young company has no brand to damage.
principles.quote: you can do aggressive and outrageous things, uh you know, months into creating your company because there's no brand to destroy.

principles.text: Build the buyers while you build the product, so you launch with customers or stop early.
principles.quote: you need to be building the buyers at the same time. And it just de-risks your startup journey tremendously

principles.text: Founder brand lifts every other channel, so treat it as a long-run commitment rather than judging it by monthly demos.
principles.quote: the biggest determinant of the of an open rate of an email is who sends it.

principles.text: Bootstrap discipline should not be dropped when scaling; acting like a VC-backed CEO and hiring seniors without processes hurt badly.
principles.quote: I totally lost that, and I started behaving like a venture-backed CEO.
